core_obligations: Derive (2) from (1) by induction on n, beginning with n = 2: from a_1 f_1 + a_2 f_2 = 1 find a covering on which a_1 f_1 or a_2 f_2 is invertible, hence f_1 or f_2 is invertible (proof lines 7652-7659).
Extend the induction to n > 2 using the Bezout relation a_1 f_1 + ... + a_n f_n = 1 and the two-element case, reducing the number of generators on a covering (proof lines 7659 onwards).

Show the equivalence with the sheaf-theoretic formulation (3) by checking the surjectivity of the displayed map on a covering, and close the cycle by noting (2) implies (1) (remaining lines up to 7686).
proof_roadmap: Reduce the finite family statement to the two-element case by induction.
Handle the two-element case by a covering and a Bezout relation.
Translate the combinatorial statement into surjectivity of the displayed map of sheaves.
difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the equivalence of three formulations of the locally ringed condition on a ringed site: the pointwise dichotomy for a single section, the finite family version for sections generating the unit ideal, and the surjectivity of the explicit map from two copies of O x O to O x O. The proof derives (2) from (1) by induction on n, handling n = 2 with an explicit Bezout relation a_1 f_1 + a_2 f_2 = 1 and passing to a covering on which one of the products is invertible, then reducing the general case to the two-element case (proof lines 7651-7686). The equivalence with the sheaf-theoretic formulation (3) is then obtained on a covering. H2: the induction reducing the finite family case to the Bezout case, and the translation into the surjectivity statement, are the substance and are written out.
